sections.label: Education, healthcare, transport spending
sections.summary: Spending on education, healthcare and transport has risen sharply, and Singapore is embarking on new infrastructure such as Changi Airport Terminal 5.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our spending on education in FY2016 is expected to be $12.8 billion, almost double what it was 10 years ago1.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Compared to a decade ago, our healthcare spending has increased almost six-fold to $11 billion2.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: One in eight Singaporeans is aged 65 and above currently.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This will rise to one in six by 2020, and one in four by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For our home, we must invest for better liveability and connectivity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This year, our transport spending is expected to hit $10.1 billion – more than five times what we spent a decade ago3.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: At the same time, we are embarking on new infrastructure of unprecedented scale, such as Changi Airport Terminal 5.

sections.label: Economic restructuring and productivity
sections.summary: Over five years restructuring tightened foreign worker inflow, funded productivity measures and the Transition Support Package, with productivity growth flat in the past three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Over the past five years, our economic restructuring journey has focused on raising productivity to achieve quality growth: (a) we tightened the inflow of foreign workers; (b) we invested significantly in broad-based measures, such as the Productivity and Innovation Credit (PIC); and (c) we introduced the Transition Support Package4 to help firms adjust to economic restructuring and rising business costs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For instance, a survey has shown that around nine in 10 of our small and medium enterprises (SMEs) embarked on productivity initiatives5 in 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The net inflow of foreign workers has slowed significantly from nearly 80,000 in 2011 to less than 23,000 in 20156.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: With a tighter labour market, we managed to sustain real median income growth for Singaporeans at an average of 2.9%7 per year over 2009 to 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: While productivity has grown by an average of 2.7% per year over 2009 to 20158, most of this increase was due to a cyclical rebound in 2010 and 2011.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Productivity growth has remained relatively flat over the past three years9.

sections.label: Unemployment and GDP growth
sections.summary: Unemployment remained low at 1.9%, and MTI expects GDP to grow 1% to 3% for the year, similar to 2% in 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: At the same time, however, unemployment remained low at 1.9%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In summary, while we face weaker prospects overall, the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) expects GDP to grow at 1% to 3% for the year, not very different from the 2% in 201510.

sections.label: Asian growth opportunities
sections.summary: China, India and ASEAN are expected to grow 6.3% per year over the next five years, accounting for more than half of global growth.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: While there are challenges, there are also growing opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We are in the centre of the Asian growth story: China, India and ASEAN are expected to grow at 6.3%11 per year over the next five years, accounting for more than half of global growth12.

sections.label: Fiscal impulse and Industry Transformation
sections.summary: The Budget gives a positive fiscal impulse of slightly over 1% of GDP, and the Industry Transformation Programme will strengthen enterprises and industry.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Taking into account the higher expenditures and additional measures introduced in this Budget, our projection is that this will amount to a positive fiscal impulse of slightly over 1% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Second, as increased spending alone cannot address structural issues, we will target resources towards enabling firms to build deeper capabilities, develop their people, scale up and internationalise.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will launch the Industry Transformation Programme to strengthen enterprises and industry and to drive growth through innovation.

sections.label: Corporate Income Tax Rebate increase
sections.summary: The Corporate Income Tax Rebate is raised from 30% to 50% of tax payable, capped at $20,000 yearly for YAs 2016 and 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Second, to help companies, especially SMEs, I will raise the existing Corporate Income Tax (CIT) Rebate, from 30% of tax payable to 50% of tax payable, with a cap of $20,000 rebate each year for Year of Assessments (YAs) 2016 and 2017.

sections.label: Special Employment Credit and SME loans
sections.summary: SEC is modified and extended to 2019 with a $1.1 billion top-up, and an SME Working Capital Loan scheme offers loans up to $300,000 per SME.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our third measure to support companies is the Special Employment Credit (SEC).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will modify and extend SEC for three years, to the end of 2019, to provide employers with a wage offset for workers aged 55 and above and earning up to $4,000 a month16.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Employers with Singaporean workers aged 65 and above will continue to receive a wage offset of up to 8%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The SEC will be up to 5% for workers aged 60 to 64 and up to 3% for those aged 55 to 59.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The SEC will cover about 340,000 workers, or about three in four older Singaporean workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To support this extension, I will top up the SEC Fund by $1.1 billion   The fourth measure will support viable SMEs that may have cash flow concerns or wish to continue growing their business.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will introduce an SME Working Capital Loan scheme, for loans of up to $300,000 per SME.

sections.label: Business Grants Portal launch
sections.summary: The Business Grants Portal will be launched in the fourth quarter of this year to be more enterprise-centric.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To be more enterprise-centric, we will launch the Business Grants Portal in the fourth quarter of this year.

sections.label: Automation Support Package
sections.summary: A new Automation Support Package will be offered for an initial three years to support companies to automate, drive productivity and scale up.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To support companies to automate, drive productivity and scale up, we will offer a new Automation Support Package for an initial period of three years.

sections.label: Automation Support Package details
sections.summary: The package provides grants up to 50% of project cost capped at $1 million, a 100% Investment Allowance, and risk-share enhanced from 50% to 70%, with over $400 million support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: First, we will provide a grant to support the roll-out or scaling up of automation projects.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will fund these projects up to 50% of project cost, with a maximum grant of $1 million.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Second, for qualifying projects, there will be a new 100% Investment Allowance for automation equipment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To do so, the Government will enhance our risk-share with participating financial institutions from 50% to 70% for such projects.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This comprehensive package offered by the Automation Support Package will be useful to firms seeking to grow.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We anticipate that the Automation Support Package will provide support of over $400 million over the next three years.

sections.label: M&A allowance and equity gains
sections.summary: M&A allowance is 25% of deal value up to $10 million per Year of Assessment, and non-taxation of gains on equity disposals is extended to 31 May 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: With the enhancement of the M&A allowance to 25% of the value of the deal as announced in Budget 2015, companies can now enjoy up to $10 million of M&A tax allowances per Year of Assessment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To provide upfront certainty to companies for their corporate restructuring, I will extend the non-taxation of companies' gains on disposal of their equity investments, based on existing scheme parameters, until 31 May 2022.

sections.label: Internationalisation support and tax deduction
sections.summary: IE supported 34,000 companies in 2015, a 21% increase over 2014, and the Double Tax Deduction for Internationalisation scheme is extended to 31 March 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In 2015, IE supported 34,000 companies in their internationalisation efforts, a 21% increase over 2014.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In addition, I will extend the Double Tax Deduction for Internationalisation scheme until 31 March 2020.

sections.label: NTP development cost
sections.summary: NTP is expected to cost more than $100 million to develop.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: NTP is expected to cost more than $100 million to develop.

sections.label: National Robotics Programme funding
sections.summary: Over $450 million will support the National Robotics Programme over the next three years, working with solution providers to offer packaged solutions to SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will now scale up our efforts and, in particular, work with solution providers to offer packaged solutions to SMEs at a reasonable cost.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will make available over $450 million to support the National Robotics Programme over the next three years.

sections.label: SPRING and TAC projects
sections.summary: SPRING will partner TACs on 30 projects over three years to reach over 3,000 SMEs, with up to $30 million over five years for TAC capabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: SPRING will partner TACs to drive 30 such projects over the next three years, to reach out to more than 3,000 SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will set aside up to $30 million over the next five years to support TACs in developing their capabilities, with additional funding for industry-wide transformation projects23.

sections.label: RIE 2020 industry-research collaboration
sections.summary: Up to $4 billion of the RIE 2020 Plan commitment will be directed to industry-research collaboration.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Of the commitment announced for the Research, Innovation and Enterprise (RIE) 2020 Plan, up to $4 billion will be directed to industry-research collaboration.

sections.label: National Research Fund top-up and IP write-down
sections.summary: A $1.5 billion top-up goes to the National Research Fund, and businesses may write down IP acquisition costs over five, 10 or 15 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To support the RIE 2020 effort, I will provide a top-up of $1.5 billion to the National Research Fund this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To encourage companies to acquire IP, I will now allow businesses the flexibility to write down the cost of acquiring IP over different periods of five, 10 or 15 years, instead of the current five years only24.

sections.label: New entity SG-Innovate
sections.summary: A new entity called "SG-Innovate" will be set up to give these efforts a further boost.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To give these efforts a further boost, we will set up a new entity called "SG-Innovate".

sections.label: Industry Transformation Programme funding
sections.summary: A total of $4.5 billion is set aside under the Industry Transformation Programme to support enterprises and industries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As a whole, I will set aside a total of $4.5 billion27 under the Industry Transformation Programme to support enterprises and industries, on top of the amounts for R&D and National Productivity Fund.

sections.label: Food Manufacturing sector support
sections.summary: Over $300 million goes to the Food Manufacturing sector over five years, with an integrated approach across more than 20 sectors covering around 80% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For example, we will make available over $300 million to the Food Manufacturing sector over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This includes support to firms and TACs, as well as initiatives, such as specialised industrial infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will take this more integrated and more targeted approach, in partnership with industry, across more than 20 sectors, covering around 80% of our GDP.

sections.label: PIC payout rate lowered
sections.summary: The PIC cash payout rate is lowered from 60% to 40% for expenditures from 1 August 2016, and the scheme expires after YA 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In line with our move towards more targeted measures, I will lower the cash payout rate under PIC from the current 60% to 40% for expenditures incurred on or after 1 August 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The PIC scheme, which has been extended for YA 2016 to YA 2018, will expire thereafter.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In addition to the Industry Transformation Programme, I will also extend and strengthen tax incentives to encourage higher industrial land productivity and to enhance activities in the areas of finance and treasury, global trading and maritime activities.

sections.label: Adapt and Grow employment support
sections.summary: MOM will enhance employment support through the "Adapt and Grow" initiative to help people amid softening economic conditions and restructuring.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To support our people amidst softening economic conditions and ongoing restructuring, the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) will enhance employment support through the "Adapt and Grow" initiative.

sections.label: PMET job matching with SMEs
sections.summary: Outreach for PMETs is expected to more than double from 2,000 to over 4,000, with MOM committing an additional $35 million a year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will also enhance efforts to help match them in jobs with SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We expect to more than double the current outreach for professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMETs) from 2,000 to over 4,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: MOM will commit an additional $35 million a year from the Lifelong Learning Endowment Fund and Skills Development Fund to support these initiatives.

sections.label: TechSkills Accelerator for ICT
sections.summary: The TechSkills Accelerator is set up as a skills development and job placement hub for the ICT sector.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The average starting pay of fresh computer engineering graduates increased by over 14% last year to around $4,000 for fresh graduates.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Infocomm Development Authority of Singapore (IDA) estimates that we will have about 30,000 new positions by 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To enable our people to learn new ICT skills quickly, we will set up the TechSkills Accelerator, a new skills development and job placement hub for the ICT sector.

sections.label: First Step CDA grant
sections.summary: A new Child Development Account First Step grant gives all Singaporean children $3,000 automatically for healthcare and childcare needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: I will, first, speak about the measures for our young – First Step, KidSTART and Fresh Start.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We will introduce a new Child Development Account (CDA) First Step grant for all Singaporean children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Parents will automatically receive $3,000 in their child's CDA, which they can use for their children's healthcare and childcare needs.

sections.label: MediSave pre-delivery withdrawal limit
sections.summary: Higher matching grants are available, and the MediSave withdrawal limit for pre-delivery medical expenses doubles from $450 to $900 immediately.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: They can receive higher matching grants, as shown in the table  .

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We will also double the MediSave withdrawal limit for pre-delivery medical expenses, from $450 to $900, with immediate effect.

sections.label: Singapore-context pilot approaches
sections.summary: Approaches best suited to the Singapore context will be developed, with the pilot expected to cost more than $20 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We will develop approaches that work best in the Singapore context.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: This pilot is expected to cost more than $20 million.

sections.label: Fresh Start Housing Scheme grant
sections.summary: The Fresh Start Housing Scheme provides a grant of up to $35,000 for families with young children to own a 2-room flat with a shorter lease.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The Fresh Start Housing Scheme will provide a grant of up to $35,000 to help such families with young children to own a 2-room flat, with a shorter lease, which will be more affordable for them.

sections.label: OBS Coney Island campus
sections.summary: The OBS campus on Coney Island is expected to be ready around 2020 and cost about $250 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The OBS campus on Coney Island is expected to be ready around 2020 and cost about $250 million.

sections.label: WIS and training support changes
sections.summary: From January 2017 WIS qualifying income ceiling rises to $2,000 a month, benefiting about 460,000 Singaporeans, alongside Workfare Training Support and SkillsFuture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: They can also upgrade their skills through the Workfare Training Support scheme and SkillsFuture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We will further improve WIS for work done from January 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: First, we will raise the qualifying income ceiling from the current average wage of $1,900 a month, to $2,000 a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: In total, we expect WIS to benefit about 460,000 Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: For example, workers earning $1,000 to $1,600 a month29 will receive increases in payouts of $100 to $500 per year.

sections.label: WIS budget enhancements
sections.summary: With these enhancements to WIS, the total budget will be about $770 million a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: With these enhancements to WIS, the total budget will be about $770 million a year.

sections.label: CPF contributions criterion
sections.summary: Seniors with not more than $70,000 in total CPF contributions by age 55 meet the first criterion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Seniors who have not more than $70,000 in total CPF contributions by age 55 will meet the first criterion.

sections.label: Silver Support eligibility and payouts
sections.summary: Seniors in the bottom one-third of households earning not more than $1,100 per member monthly can receive $300 to $750 quarterly, depending on flat type.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Seniors in the bottom one-third of households where, on average, each member earns not more than $1,100 per month, can benefit from Silver Support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Eligible seniors will receive between $300 and $750 every quarter, depending on their flat type   The majority of seniors living in 1- and 2-room flats will receive Silver Support.

sections.label: Couple's Silver Support payouts
sections.summary: The couple would receive $600 each every three months, or $4,800 together over the year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The couple would receive $600 each in Silver Support payouts every three months, or $4,800 together over the whole year.

sections.label: First Silver Support payout timing
sections.summary: The first payout will be in July this year, a double payout for April to June and July to September 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: As this is a new and extensive scheme, we needed more time to operationalise it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We will make the first payout in July this year, and it will be a double payout for two quarters – the two quarters of April to June 2016, and July to September 2016.

sections.label: Silver Support beneficiaries and cost
sections.summary: Silver Support will benefit more than 140,000 seniors and cost close to $320 million in the first year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Silver Support will benefit more than 140,000 seniors and will cost close to $320 million in the first year.

sections.label: Community Networks for Seniors pilot
sections.summary: The government will pilot Community Networks for Seniors to better support leaders like Lucy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: To better support leaders like Lucy, we will pilot Community Networks for Seniors.

sections.label: Higher public assistance and pensions
sections.summary: Basic monthly cash allowance will rise, with a two-person public assistance household receiving $80 more monthly, totalling $870, and the Singapore Allowance and pension ceiling will each increase by $20.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Public Assistance recipients also often receive assistance in cash, food delivery and other vouchers from community-based agencies and grassroots volunteers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We will raise the basic monthly cash allowance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: For example, a two-person household, where both are on public assistance, will now receive an additional $80 a month, bringing the total amount of cash assistance per month to $870.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: To help Government pensioners who draw lower pensions, the Government will increase the Singapore Allowance and monthly pension ceiling by $20 per month – to $300 and $1,230 respectively.

sections.label: GSTV cash and S&CC rebates
sections.summary: The one-off GSTV Cash special payment will cost $280 million in 2016 and benefit 1.4 million Singaporeans, while S&CC rebates costing $86 million will benefit about 840,000 HDB households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The one-off GSTV – Cash special payment will cost an additional $280 million in 2016 and benefit 1.4 million Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We will also provide one to three months of service and conservancy charges (S&CC) rebate: 1- and 2-room HDB households will receive a total of three months of rebates for this year, while 3- and 4-room households will receive two months of rebates   This will cost the Government $86 million and benefit about 840,000 HDB households.

sections.label: Cap on personal income tax relief
sections.summary: A cap of $80,000 per Year of Assessment will be introduced on the total personal income tax relief an individual can claim.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: However, taken together, the tax reliefs may unduly reduce total taxable incomes for a small proportion of individuals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: I will introduce a cap on the total amount of personal income tax relief an individual can claim, at $80,000 per YA.

sections.label: Our Singapore Fund for SG50 projects
sections.summary: A new fund called Our Singapore Fund will be set up to support citizens like Seema, Harsha, Dennis and Wilson who created SG50 projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: To support passionate citizens like Seema, Harsha, Dennis and Wilson, and many others like them who created a whole array of meaningful SG50 projects, we will set up a new fund called Our Singapore Fund.

sections.label: Fund size and setup date
sections.summary: The total fund size will be up to $25 million and it will be set up by the second half of 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The total fund size will be up to $25 million and it will be set up by the second half of 2016.

sections.label: Budget deficit and spending
sections.summary: FY2015 Budget is expected to record a $4.9 billion deficit, and FY2016 total spending is expected to be $5 billion higher than FY2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: For FY2015, our Budget is expected to record a deficit of $4.9 billion or 1.2% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: In FY2016, total spending is expected to be $5 billion or 7.3% higher than in FY2015.

sections.label: Temasek added to NIR
sections.summary: This year Temasek will be added to the NIR framework and will be a long-term source of revenue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: In addition, this year, Temasek will be added to our NIR framework and this will be a source of revenue for the long term.

sections.label: Reviewing expenditure and surplus
sections.summary: Major expenditure items will be reviewed for efficiency and effectiveness, with an expected overall budget surplus of $3.4 billion in the first year of the term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We will review the major expenditure items we expect ahead to ensure efficiency and effectiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We expect an overall budget surplus of $3.4 billion or 0.8% of GDP in this first year of the term.

sections.label: Industry Transformation Programme
sections.summary: The economy will be transformed through the Industry Transformation Programme, emphasising enterprise and innovation, marking a new phase in economic restructuring.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We will also set our sights on the long term and position ourselves to stand out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We will transform our economy through the Industry Transformation Programme, emphasising enterprise and innovation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: This marks a new phase in our economic restructuring.

sections.label: Future economy and social schemes
sections.summary: The Committee on the Future Economy will examine preparing the economy for the future, alongside Silver Support, Community Networks for Seniors, and schemes for the young.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The Committee on the Future Economy will dive deep into what we must do to get our economy ready for the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Silver Support is a major new step to help seniors with lesser means.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The Community Networks for Seniors will forge a new way to care for our seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: First Step, KidSTART, Fresh Start, OBS@Coney – these are our investments in our young.

sections.label: Parliament debate adjourned
sections.summary: The Question seeks Parliament's approval of the Government's financial policy for 1 April 2016 to 31 March 2017, and the debate stands adjourned.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Speaker
sentences.text: The Question is, "That Parliament approves the financial policy of the Government for the financial year 1 April 2016 to 3129 30M31a32rch 2017." In accordance with paragraph (1) of Standing Order No 89, the debate now stands adjourned.
